subject: Request: temporary SLO carve-out for migration weekend
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@brightplanet.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: legal@brightplanet.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary SLO carve-out request for migration weekend

Hi Dylan,

We have a planned migration of our analytics pipeline the weekend of June 5–6. During a 10-hour maintenance window (Saturday 00:00–10:00 PT) we anticipate elevated maintenance tasks that will require extended access to site operations and will temporarily increase alert noise. Our SRE lead asked whether Redwood can approve a temporary change to our support response targets for that window: specifically, relax P2 response from 4 hours to 8 hours and allow P1 initial response up to 60 minutes instead of the standard 30.

We want to avoid repeated page escalations for known maintenance activity, but still need a clear escalation path if customer-facing impact or data-loss indicators appear. Attached is our migration runbook and a short exception form.

Can you confirm whether this is possible and what approvals you need? Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the plan.

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Director of Ops, BrightPlanet
attachments: BP-migration-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet), SLO-exception-form.pdf (form)
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@brightplanet.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary SLO carve-out request for migration weekend

Alicia — thanks for the heads up and for sending the runbook.

Quick summary of next steps from our side: 
- I'll open an internal exception request and route to Ops/Support leadership for a timeboxed approval.
- Need a single point of contact on your side during the window (name + mobile pager).
- We will keep the P1 escalation path intact (pager -> on-call -> engineering lead) but can extend the first response SLA to 60m for the scheduled window only.
- P2 relaxation to 8h is doable, but will require approval from Support leadership due to SLA-term implications.

Can you add the SRE contact in a follow-up and confirm whether the migration contains any schema-change that could cause data loss? That will affect the approvals we need.

I looped in Ben and Marissa to expedite approvals.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.com
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary SLO carve-out request for migration weekend

On Mon, 31 May 2027 at 08:03 -0700, dylan_brooks@redwood.com wrote:
> Alicia — thanks for the heads up and for sending the runbook.

Dylan — quick operational note: we can approve P1 initial response at 60m for a scheduled maintenance window, but we need a runbook checkpoint at T+2h and an automated telemetry threshold that re-triggers full escalation if error-rate or sustained latency crosses our thresholds. We should capture that as a clause in the exception form.

Marissa — can you ok the P2 relaxation to 8h for BrightPlanet? This is a larger policy exception and I'll need a sign-off from Support leadership.

Also tagging Mina to confirm on-call coverage overlap with APAC (BrightPlanet has global users).

-Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Support Ops
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary SLO carve-out request for migration weekend

Ben — I reviewed the runbook. We can approve the P2 relaxation to 8h limited to the 10-hour maintenance window provided all of the following are met: 

- BrightPlanet provides a named on-site SRE + mobile contact and confirms no schema-change that risks irreversible data loss.
- Runbook includes an explicit rollback plan and checkpoint at T+2h (we will call this out in the exception).
- Automated telemetry alert (error rate >1% sustained for 5m, or 99th latency >3x baseline) must trigger immediate full escalation.
- Legal accepts the temporary amendment to SLO terms (I see legal is CC'd).

If those are satisfied I approve the carve-out. Ben/Mina, please prepare the exception form and ops playbook bullet points.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Support & Customer Experience
Redwood Inference
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@brightplanet.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com, legal@brightplanet.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary SLO carve-out request for migration weekend

Alicia — thanks, approved pending the two confirmations below.

Please reply with the following in this thread: 
1) Named SRE contact + mobile/cell number who will be reachable during the window.
2) Confirmation that the migration contains no irreversible schema changes or if it does, the exact rollback step(s).

Once you reply we'll update the SLO-exception-form (attached) with the telemetry thresholds and T+2h checkpoint, and I'll route to Legal for a short amendment sign-off. We will also add an automated gateway check in Redwood Console to re-open full escalation if the telemetry thresholds breach.

If easier, we can do a 15-min pre-window alignment call on Friday — available 9:30am or 3:00pm PT.

Thanks — looking forward to the confirmations so we can finalize.

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: SLO-exception-form.pdf (fillable PDF)
